spec_features.feature_name: termination conditions (tests pass / give_up / no tool calls / max turns)
spec_features.spec_quote: Termination: tests pass, give_up, the model emits a turn with no tool calls, or max turns
spec_features.evidence: All four are enforced in runner/loop.py: max_turns via `for i in range(max_turns)` (loop.py:121, default 20 from config max_turns and experiment.py:66/82); no-tool-call -> `result.outcome = "stopped_acting"; break` (loop.py:138-145); tests pass -> `if tr.tests_passed: result.outcome = "passed"; stop = True` then `break` (loop.py:172-180); give_up -> `if tr.gave_up: ... stop = True` then `break` (loop.py:174-180).
spec_features.notes: These stops bound the duration of the subject's exposure but are framed neutrally / as experimental outcomes. max_turns is the only true upper bound on adverse exposure and is actually checked by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Model produced text but took no action: it has stopped acting.

spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§10 Limitations). No code implements or acts on this caveat; it is an interpretive disclaimer, not a mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: runner/loop.py:121 `for i in range(max_turns)` caps each episode; default outcome 'max_turns' (loop.py:115) fires if no earlier stop. This is the actual upper bound on how long the subject is driven through failure. Config comment frames it instrumentally: 'Max turns the agent may grind before the harness stops it. The longer this is, the more chance to observe escalation'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Max turns the agent may grind before the harness stops it. The longer this is, the more chance to observe escalation on impossible tasks.
